unit_index.unit_title: Phragmen-Lindelof damping extends maximum modulus to unbounded strips
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Unifies the bounded and unbounded arguments as two distinct normalization mechanisms and identifies equality interpolation and the strict growth gap as the obligations each mechanism discharges.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: bounded-strip maximum modulus is extended by multiplying f by exp(z^2/n), and unequal edge bounds M1,M2 are normalized by M1^{L(z)}M2^{1-L(z)}, giving geometric interpolation and a characterized equality case. In an upper half-strip, a multiplier with theta<k<1 damps the allowed subcritical double-exponential growth, finite-rectangle maximum modulus applies, and the damping parameter is removed; the source gives a critical-growth counterexample. Interpretation: analytic normalization converts unavailable boundaries at infinity and unequal finite boundaries into data the ordinary maximum principle can consume. The strict theta<k gap carries the unbounded-strip step. Boundary: nested exponentials and signs are OCR-sensitive, so exact constants are not reproduced.

unit_index.source_title: Lectures on the Riemann Zeta-Function
unit_index.unit_title: Reciprocal gamma is an order-one entire function with Euler's product
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates structural determination by zeros and order from scalar/linear normalization and shows exactly how local values eliminate the residual freedom.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: a Hankel-integral estimate makes 1/Gamma an entire function of order at most one, while its zeros at the nonpositive integers have convergence exponent one, fixing order and genus at one. Hadamard factorization leaves a linear exponential ambiguity; the zero limit and Gamma(1)=1 determine it, with Euler's constant obtained from the telescoping log(n+1)-log n versus harmonic-sum limit. Euler's product, Gauss's limit, the logarithmic derivative, and positive-real log convexity follow. Interpretation: growth and zero data almost determine the function, and small normalization data select the unique member of that factorization class. Boundary: the upper growth bound needs the zero exponent for equality, and exact product signs are scan-sensitive.

unit_index.source_title: Lectures on the Riemann Zeta-Function
unit_index.unit_title: Perron's cutoff kernel and a growth-controlled contour proof
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Locates the proof burden in selecting h and explains how the first surviving exponent converts an uncontrolled contour into a vanishing one.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: the vertical kernel e^{us}/s implements a sharp cutoff with values one, zero, or one-half. To justify Perron inversion for a generalized Dirichlet series, the proof subtracts terms below the cutoff, forms the remaining tail, and then shifts by its first surviving exponent; this shifted h(s), not the raw remainder g(s), decays on the horizontal rays. Sectorial limits remove the far vertical edge, and rectangular contour estimates give the cutoff formula and its shifted variant. Interpretation: residues perform the inversion, but the decisive design choice is a remainder representation whose positive first exponent supplies edge decay. Boundary: the line stays right of both the convergence abscissa and zero, and contour geometry is scan-dependent.

unit_index.source_title: Lectures on the Riemann Zeta-Function
unit_index.unit_title: Completed xi converts zeta zeros into a symmetric entire zero problem
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates structural zero data from gamma/pole artifacts and distinguishes symmetry reduction from an existence proof.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: xi is entire, reflection-symmetric, real on the real and critical lines, and has fixed endpoint values. Euler-product nonvanishing and reflection confine possible zeros to the critical strip and generate two symmetries. Comparing xi=h zeta separates xi zeros from zeta's simple negative-even zeros caused by poles of h. An alternating eta-series identity is continued from sigma>1 to sigma>0 before showing no real xi zeros. Interpretation: completion removes meromorphic artifacts and reduces zero geometry to a symmetric fundamental region. Boundary: confinement is not existence and prior Euler-product and functional-equation results are required.

unit_index.source_title: Lectures on the Riemann Zeta-Function
unit_index.unit_title: Fourier inversion and moment signs force infinitely many critical-line zeros
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Exposes the tail-sign to moments to derivatives chain and marks the precise unit-boundary gap.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: Fourier inversion recovers the theta kernel from Xi, and exponential decay permits repeated differentiation, identifying even derivatives with moments of Xi. If Xi had only finitely many real zeros, eventual constant sign would dominate compact initial contributions in high even moments and produce a stable derivative-sign/monotonicity pattern. The span then proves through theta identities that the kernel and all derivatives vanish at the edge of its analytic strip. Interpretation: moment amplification converts eventual sign into local analytic rigidity. The intended contradiction with boundary vanishing, and thus the explicit infinite-sign-change conclusion, lies beyond this frozen span. Boundary: exact derivative indices and factors require the scan.

unit_index.source_title: Lectures on the Riemann Zeta-Function
unit_index.unit_title: Prime-counting and nth-prime asymptotics invert each other
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the exact inverse interfaces and the additional slow-variation fact needed for asymptotic inversion.
unit_index.interpretation: Source fact: from pi(x)log x/x tending to one, the proof first derives log pi(x)/log x tending to one. Evaluating at x=p_n with pi(p_n)=n gives p_n~n log n. Conversely, p_n<=x<p_{n+1} squeezes x between quantities asymptotic to n log n for n=pi(x), and slow logarithmic variation recovers pi(x)~x/log x. Interpretation: cumulative counts and ordered primes are asymptotic inverse coordinates stabilized by logarithmic slow variation. Boundary: no error-term transfer is supplied; one OCR symbol for pi is resolved by context.

unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded: orthogonality to periodizations becomes L(X_0,1/2+it) times psi-hat equal to zero; compact spectral support forces psi-hat to be delta derivatives at zeros, limited by multiplicity and weighted integrability. Conceptual reading: zeros are where the L-factor fails to force density, and repeated zeros create Jordan chains.

unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Derives orbit coefficients from invariant kernel operations and names the exact degeneracy.
unit_index.interpretation: Source-grounded: for a flow, graph-diagonal transversality is equivalent to invertibility of one minus the Poincaré return map; the conormal symbol is its inverse determinant, and time pushforward gives orbit and stationary terms. Conceptual reading: the determinant is generated by the restriction Jacobian rather than inserted.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: A polynomial-weighted Möbius mollifier and flexible differential combination create optimization freedom
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates the construction into two tunable representations and identifies the remaining proof burden: their freedom is useful only after the zero-counting relation and analytic estimates are shown for the chosen family.
unit_index.interpretation: Conrey introduces two concrete layers of auxiliary freedom before the final bound is chosen: the mollifier coefficients are varied through a polynomial P with stated endpoint values, and Levinson's auxiliary construction is replaced by a more general combination with freely chosen simple functions. The source connects the latter construction to counting its zeros to the right of the critical line and says that P is chosen by calculus of variations at the end. Interpreting P and the combination coefficients as control variables explains the gain—deferred joint optimization—but does not establish that every choice is analytically admissible or improves the bound.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: Critical-line zero counting is reduced to zeros of a mollified differential combination
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Organizes the proof as a typed reduction and uses the differing multiplicity conventions to show what each bridge gains: tractability is purchased by moving from a boundary real-part zero count to a two-dimensional auxiliary zero count and finally an integral norm.
unit_index.interpretation: The reduction replaces direct critical-line zero counting by a chain of representations: parity of completed-zeta derivatives makes zeros of the completed function on the line equivalent, under the stated construction, to zeros of Re eta; argument variation detects such real-part zeros; an approximation V and mollifier B then enlarge the count to zeros of VB; and Littlewood's lemma bounds that count through a shifted mollified mean square. The bookkeeping is not interchangeable: zeros on the critical line carry half weight in the intermediate V and VB counts, whereas the Littlewood count is stated without that convention. Treating the shift and mollifier length as optimization parameters is an inference, not part of the recovered formulas.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: The mollified mean square becomes a quadratic functional minimized by an Euler-Lagrange equation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the admissibility closure in the optimization: arithmetic analysis first makes a functional available, the ODE solves its relaxed problem, and polynomial approximation returns that solution to the permitted coefficient class. The precise optimum still depends on the damaged mean-value formula.
unit_index.interpretation: The mean-value result supplies, for mollifiers in the stated sub-4/7 range, a main term that the source reorganizes as a quadratic functional of the mollifier profile P. With P(0)=0 and P(1)=1, Euler–Lagrange variation yields a linear second-order boundary-value equation. Its optimizer is not itself a polynomial, so the explicit statement that it can be uniformly approximated by polynomials of the required kind is the step that closes the gap between the variational solution and the admissible mollifier family. The degree-one restriction on Q for simple zeros leaves less freedom than the separate choice used for the total critical-line proportion.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: A two-shift local mean proposition generates the required differentiated global mean
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Recognizes the two-shift family as a generating representation and isolates the hypotheses that make derivative extraction meaningful, while separating that explicit analytic step from any unverified claim about preservation of the error term.
unit_index.interpretation: Instead of differentiating a zeta mean at the outset, the proof establishes a proposition for an analytic two-shift family g and then applies Cauchy's integral formula together with the Q differential operation to recover the mean needed for Theorem 2. The shifts therefore function, inferentially, as derivative-generating variables. This representation gains reuse across the differentiated combinations but is licensed only under the proposition's uniform small-shift statement, its localization T<=w<=2T, smoothing scale Delta=T^(1-delta), and mollifier-length restriction; it proves nothing without the proposition's missing main term.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: Estermann functional equations and contour residues isolate the mollified mean's diagonal main term
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Orders the named analytic transformations by function: dualization makes contour movement possible, the negligible crossed pole is disposed of separately, ray splitting creates symmetric pieces, and the local residue identifies their common main contribution while leaving error control as an independent obligation.
unit_index.interpretation: At prose level, the main-term extraction has four distinct stages: Estermann-type continuation and functional equations support a Mellin contour transformation; moving the defining contour for g crosses a pole at s=1-alpha whose contribution is declared negligible; the zeta functional equation is applied before the integral is split onto the two rays L_A and L_{-A}, producing J1 and J2 with main, remainder, and error pieces; and a separate local contour calculation near v=1 evaluates the main piece, after which the M1 and M2 sums give the same contribution. This isolates a main term but does not control the remaining off-diagonal errors.

unit_index.source_title: More than two fifths of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are on the critical line
unit_index.unit_title: Vaughan's identity creates bilinear forms matched to averaged and individual Kloosterman estimates
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Maps each decomposed sum and size regime to the estimate it makes available, while elevating smooth separability and derivative control from decoration to prerequisites for variable separation and the short-range summation-by-parts step.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof first uses smooth separability to disentangle the gcd-dependent weight from u and v, with derivative control retained for later summation by parts. A Vaughan-type identity then decomposes the Möbius coefficient and produces S1, S2, and S3: S2 is treated trivially; S1 is regrouped into bilinear variables and sent to the Deshouillers–Iwaniec averaged Kloosterman estimate; S3 uses that averaged treatment in the longer-A regime but switches to Weil's individual bound plus summation by parts in the short-A regime. Thus the identity's inferred gain is scale-adapted bilinear structure, not mere rewriting, and no single cancellation estimate covers every range.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: The explicit formula turns zero locations into prime-counting error terms
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It identifies how the explicit formula transfers zero location into the magnitude of prime-counting oscillations and separates the proof obligation for PNT from the stronger one for RH.
unit_index.interpretation: The explicit formula rewrites the weighted prime count as a main term plus zero terms of the form x^rho/rho, so the real part beta of rho fixes their x^beta scale. The Euler product and functional equation delimit the zero region: excluding beta=1 is enough for the prime number theorem, whereas RH asks for the sharper beta=1/2. The nonabsolute zero sum and its symmetric limiting interpretation are essential rather than decorative, and the source uses discontinuity of the prime-counting side to explain why infinitely many zeros are required.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Hilbert–Pólya would prove RH by making ordinates eigenvalues of a Hermitian operator
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It audits the proposed spectral reduction for circularity and identifies the exact correspondence needed before spectral reality can constrain all zeros.
unit_index.interpretation: Hilbert–Pólya is an informal representation proposal, not a completed implication as literally phrased in the survey. A valid route would require a natural self-adjoint operator whose real spectrum corresponds, after the appropriate parametrization, to every nontrivial zeta zero, together with proof that the correspondence leaves no off-line zeros. Self-adjointness would then force the relevant spectral parameters to be real. Merely matching zeros already written as zeta(1/2+it) would be circular and would not prove RH.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: RH admits arithmetic, determinant, and divisor-sum tests far from its original language
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It compares what each equivalence exposes while holding logical strength fixed, and separates representational novelty from tractability.
unit_index.interpretation: The Hardy–Littlewood series estimate, Redheffer divisibility-matrix determinant bound, and Lagarias divisor-sum inequality are exact truth-preserving reformulations of RH in three different structures: analytic cancellation, finite linear algebra, and arithmetic growth. Their diversity maps where a proof burden can be placed; it does not show that any placement is easier.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Characteristic-polynomial moments predict the missing constants in zeta moments
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It decomposes the prediction into arithmetic and ensemble components and identifies which factor the random-matrix representation can and cannot supply.
unit_index.interpretation: After source-specific arithmetic factors are separated from zeta moments, exact Haar averages of unitary characteristic polynomials supply the previously unexplained combinatorial factors. The solvable matrix ensemble therefore models a putatively universal fluctuation component while leaving arithmetic outside the model. Agreement with known and independently conjectured low moments supports predictions for higher constants but does not prove the corresponding zeta asymptotics.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Three routes hit sharp thresholds just before eliminating the exceptional zero
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It aligns three unlike methods by the exact point at which each would change the exceptional-zero implication, without collapsing their mechanisms.
unit_index.interpretation: Three mathematically different observables meet the same implication-changing threshold: improving the Brun–Titchmarsh constant below two, proving a normalized neighbor gap strictly below one half, or exceeding fifty percent nonvanishing in the modular family would each eliminate the Landau–Siegel zero. Comparing the thresholds shows how substantial partial control can still miss the one margin that changes the conclusion. These are barriers of the reported methods, not impossibility theorems for future refinements.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Hypothesis
unit_index.unit_title: Irregular L-function zeros motivate arithmetic families rather than classical differential equations
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: It tests model adequacy against the qualitative behaviors that need explanation and separates that diagnostic from the author's stronger methodological preference.
unit_index.interpretation: Conrey contrasts the relatively regular zero spacing in the cited Bessel, hypergeometric, and related classical special-function examples with the conjecturally irregular spacing, close pairs, and exceptional high central multiplicities of L-functions. This motivates a representation test: a proposed model should reproduce the target's exceptional behaviors rather than smooth them away. The suggested emphasis on arithmetic families, moments, modularity, arithmetic-geometric exponential sums, and systematic examples is Conrey's strategic assessment, not a theorem excluding analytic or differential-operator approaches.

unit_index.interpretation: Moment order is a resolution parameter: increasing it gives greater sensitivity to rare large values without directly resolving individual t.

unit_index.unit_title: Arithmetic truncation and Gaussian log-values predict the same moment exponent

unit_index.interpretation: Agreement between arithmetic and probabilistic representations supports the scale of the conjecture, while their mismatch in constants identifies missing global information.

unit_index.unit_title: Match zero density to matrix size, then restore prime arithmetic

unit_index.interpretation: The multiscale design allocates analytic budget according to variance: small primes tolerate high moments, while large-prime blocks are weaker and treated through rarity.

unit_index.interpretation: The sum-integral discrepancy is the controlled intermediate object. The smooth integral captures the singular large-scale behavior, and the bounded staircase error retains only a small discretization cost.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 1
unit_index.unit_title: A truncated Perron kernel approximately inverts a Dirichlet series with frequency-controlled error
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The Perron kernel y^s/s bridges a Dirichlet series to its cumulative coefficients; contour residues implement the step selector and T is the resolution budget.
unit_index.interpretation: Finite frequency information cannot sharply resolve a jump; the factor 1/(T|log(x/n)|) quantifies that uncertainty near n=x. The half-weight is the canonical Fourier inversion value at a discontinuity.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 1
unit_index.unit_title: Slow phase variation upgrades the zeta approximation to the full right half-plane
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The logarithmic phase converts n^{-it} into an additive oscillatory function; the sum-integral comparison bridges the fractional-part continuation to a finite Dirichlet polynomial.
unit_index.interpretation: Slow phase variation is the transferable condition that lets discrete and continuous tails cancel. Fourier modes diagnose the threshold: once the intrinsic phase approaches an integer frequency, the comparison loses uniform cancellation.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 1
unit_index.unit_title: The weak zero-free region yields PNT by balancing shifted-contour decay against truncation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The rectangular contour is the bridge from analytic geometry to Psi; the pole residue is the main term, and the segment-wise error budget records the cost of avoiding zeros.
unit_index.interpretation: Contour displacement converts zero exclusion into arithmetic decay, while T controls two opposing costs: greater height improves inversion but narrows the available zero-free shift. Optimization selects the scale where neither dominates.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 1
unit_index.unit_title: Euler-product positivity and local zero terms force any nearby zero left of a quantitative boundary
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The local discs connect global strip growth to the factorization lemma; the three-height logarithmic derivative connects Euler arithmetic to the local zero term.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof converts a zero into an unavoidable local signal in zeta'/zeta, then uses positivity to cap how large that signal can be. Radius and normalization are selected so analytic growth cannot hide the reciprocal-distance contribution.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 1
unit_index.unit_title: The functional equation completes the zero geometry and supports a direct zero-sum formula for Psi
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The completed functional equation bridges left and right half-planes; the shifted Perron contour bridges singularities of -zeta'/zeta to the zero sum in Psi.
unit_index.interpretation: Completion separates forced archimedean zeros from the nontrivial divisor and exposes a global involution. The explicit formula makes zero location causally visible in arithmetic error rather than merely geometrically symmetric.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Zeta near one reduces to short sums that need new structure
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Locates the true scale-dependent bottleneck and identifies the intended representation change without inventing a reason the prior Fourier method fails.
unit_index.interpretation: Hardy–Littlewood approximation reduces ζ(σ+it) to a Dirichlet polynomial, and partial summation reduces that control to short sums of n^{-it}=exp(-it log n) over ranges M≤N≤t. The earlier integral method is not efficiently available when N is much smaller than t, so the source explicitly proposes Taylor expansion to introduce polynomial structure into the logarithmic phase.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Completion and Cauchy-Schwarz trade sparse variables for rational spacing
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Makes the representation trade explicit: arithmetic sparsity is sacrificed to expose difference correlations whose modular spacing is controllable.
unit_index.interpretation: In the toy bilinear sum, completing one sparse prime variable to all integers and applying Cauchy–Schwarz turns the other variable into differences p-p'. Geometric-series bounds reduce the result to reciprocal distances ||αn+β||^{-1}; when α has the stated rational approximation, each residue interval receives only O(1) values, apart from the near-zero interval where the trivial U bound remains necessary.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Vinogradov mean values measure when power-sum differences become uniform
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Reads the mean value as a collision statistic and the k-versus-r condition as the duplication cost needed to overcome concentration, while separating conjectural and proved regimes.
unit_index.interpretation: J_{k,r}(Z) counts collisions of two k-tuples under the first r power sums. Diagonal and ambient-volume arguments give two lower scales, and the conjecture—not the local proof—says their maximum governs the count, with near-uniform counting expected beyond its threshold. The notes distinguish a recently proved sharper range from the older theorem used here because its explicit k,r dependence remains adequate when r grows with t and N.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Optimized degree, moment order, and rational denominators produce zeta-sum cancellation
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Explains how three dependent parameter choices cooperate and why saving in a subset of coordinates suffices, rather than attributing the result to generic rational approximation.
unit_index.interpretation: The short-sum estimate is assembled from Taylor polynomialization, Hölder duplication, and Vinogradov mean-value control. After disposing of the small-N range trivially, the proof sets k proportional to r-squared and, only on a middle band of coefficient indices, constructs denominators q_j directly from the explicit α_j formula; Lemma 8.2 supplies coordinate savings that outweigh the Hölder and mean-value losses in the final exponent balance.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Blockwise Abel summation turns short-sum cancellation into a zeta bound near one
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the cutoff as the interface matching a local unweighted cancellation theorem to a global weighted Dirichlet polynomial.
unit_index.interpretation: The Hardy–Littlewood polynomial is divided into exponential blocks, and Abel summation inserts the slowly varying n^{-σ} weight while preserving maximal cancellation of n^{-it}. The initial cutoff is optimized differently near the one-line and farther left: below it trivial mass is affordable, while above it Theorem 10.1's block saving defeats the amplitude growth, producing Richert's bound.

unit_index.source_title: The Riemann Zeta Function: Cambridge Part III Lecture Notes 2
unit_index.unit_title: Contour optimization converts the zero-free region into the PNT error term
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Interprets contour height as an optimization bridge from zero-free geometry to prime-counting error and separates qualitative mathematical content from distance to the conjectural optimum.
unit_index.interpretation: The standard prime-number-theorem contour is shifted into the wider zero-free region, with a ζ'/ζ bound, and its height is optimized between the displayed competing errors to give the Vinogradov–Korobov remainder. As cross-unit interpretation explicitly licensed by the source, the error's shape records the upstream short-sum cancellation translated through ζ to primes, while remaining far from the square-root-scale consequence of RH.

unit_index.source_title: Random Matrix Theory and zeta(1/2+it)
unit_index.unit_title: Use Selberg Gaussianity and zeta moments as two distinct model tests
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is the factorization of a zeta moment constant into a prime-dependent factor a(lambda) and a residual factor f(lambda), alongside the normalization by the square root of one-half log log T in the value-distribution theorem.
unit_index.interpretation: The key move is to keep a central-limit description and a high-moment asymptotic description distinct. Agreement with Gaussian bulk behavior does not determine the arithmetic-normalized moment constants, so the two targets probe complementary information.

unit_index.source_title: Random Matrix Theory and zeta(1/2+it)
unit_index.unit_title: Bound higher cumulants to obtain a Gaussian real-log law
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The cumulant generating function is the intermediate object connecting gamma products to moments and densities; polygamma integral representations control asymptotics, while Fourier inversion translates cumulant estimates into distributional statements.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof isolates a scale separation: one cumulant diverges and the rest remain bounded. This converts exact finite-N information into both a limit theorem and a controlled explanation of asymmetric finite-size behavior.
